llm.reply:
## Molecular Function

KRAS encodes a protein belonging to the small GTPase superfamily [11: "encodes a protein that is a member of the small GTPase superfamily"]. The gene product functions as a molecular switch that cycles between active GTP-bound and inactive GDP-bound states, regulating downstream signaling pathways that control cell proliferation and survival [26: "acts as a molecular switch to persistently stimulate downstream signaling pathways, including cell proliferation and survival"]. This GTPase activity is central to its normal cellular function and its oncogenic potential when mutated.

## Oncogenic Activation

A single amino acid substitution produces an activating mutation that results in a transforming protein implicated in various malignancies [11: "A single amino acid substitution is responsible for an activating mutation. The transforming protein that results is implicated in various malignancies"]. The constitutively active mutant KRAS protein drives tumorigenesis by persistently stimulating proliferative and survival signals [26: "mutations result in constitutive activation of the KRAS protein"]. Mutations in KRAS are found in approximately 40% of colorectal cancers and up to 90% of pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas [26: "mutations in approximately 40% of all CRC cases"][29: "mutated in up to 90% of all pancreatic ductal adenocarcinomas (PDACs)"].

## Therapeutic Targeting

Historically considered "undruggable," KRAS has recently become targetable through allele-specific inhibitors [27: "KRAS has been deemed a challenging therapeutic target, even 'undruggable'"][27: "surprising advances in directly targeted drugs for KRAS, especially in KRAS (G12C) inhibitors"]. Small-molecule degraders now offer a broader approach, potently degrading 13 of 17 prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles and inducing tumor regression in vivo [30: "designed a heterobifunctional small molecule that potently degrades 13 out of 17 of the most prevalent oncogenic KRAS alleles"][30: "Pharmacological degradation of oncogenic KRAS was tolerated and led to tumor regression in vivo"].
